No Key Points Expected Marking Scheme CO 17 Discuss the relevance of internet of things (IOT) in modern society, including its benefits and challenges. Define IoT, importance in society, 4–5 benefits (automation, efficiency, health, environment), 3–4 challenges (privacy, cost, standardization). Typical answer: The Internet of Things (IoT) has revolutionized how humans interact with technology, merging the physical and digital worlds. It connects everyday objects to the Internet, allowing them to sense, communicate, and act intelligently. Benefits: IoT offers automation and efficiency by enabling smart homes, intelligent transportation, precision agriculture, and health-monitoring systems. It optimizes energy usage, reduces human effort, and improves productivity in industries. For instance, smart grids balance power supply and demand automatically. Challenges: Despite its advantages, IoT faces issues such as data security, privacy violations, lack of standardization, and power management for low-energy devices. Additionally, initial setup costs and network reliability are concerns in developing regions. The digitalRead() function reads the push-button status (LOW when pressed), while digitalWrite() controls the LED state. Serial.begin() initializes serial communication, and Serial.println() prints messages for debugging. This simple control mechanism demonstrates the fundamentals of human–machine interaction in IoT systems. 20 Describe the advantages and limitations of ESP32 Wi-Fi networking compared to other IoT connectivity options. Compare ESP32 Wi-Fi with ZigBee, LoRa, Bluetooth; cover speed, range, power, cost, applications; discuss pros & cons. Typical answer: The ESP32 is a dual-core microcontroller with built-in Wi-Fi and Bluetooth, widely used in IoT systems for its speed and flexibility. It enables fast data transfer up to 150 Mbps, making it ideal for smart homes, monitoring dashboards, and automation projects requiring real-time connectivity. Compared with other technologies, ESP32 Wi-Fi provides higher data rates than Bluetooth Low Energy (BLE) or ZigBee, though it consumes more power. LoRa, in contrast, covers several kilometers but offers very low data speed, making it suitable for long-range environmental sensing. The advantages of ESP32 Wi-Fi include its integrated wireless hardware, easy Internet connectivity through a full TCP/IP stack, and strong developer support.
